votes.plain_language: This bill authorizes the President to bar from U.S. entry any vessel that has transited a port or marine terminal that was nationalized or expropriated by a Western Hemisphere country that has a free trade agreement with the United States. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass — ROTOR Act (S 2503)
votes.bill_title: ROTOR Act
votes.plain_language: This bill addresses aviation safety by increasing requirements for aircraft tracking and communication using Automatic Dependent Surveillance-Broadcast (ADS-B) technology and expanding oversight. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass — ARTIST Act (S 254)
votes.bill_title: ARTIST Act
votes.plain_language: This bill prohibits states from imposing bans on marine mammal products produced by Alaska Natives. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass — Tribal Trust Land Homeownership Act (S 723)
votes.bill_title: Tribal Trust Land Homeownership Act of 2025
votes.plain_language: This bill sets forth requirements for the processing of a proposed residential leasehold mortgage, business leasehold mortgage, land mortgage, or right-of-way document by the Bureau of Indian Affairs. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: Passage, Objections of the President To The Contrary Notwithstanding — Miccosukee Reserved Area Amendments Act (H R 504)
votes.bill_title: Miccosukee Reserved Area Amendments Act
votes.plain_language: This bill expands the Miccosukee Reserved Area to include the part of Everglades National Park known as Osceola Camp and directs the Interior Department to protect structures there from flooding. The President vetoed it, so this was a vote to override the veto, which needs two-thirds. A Yea votes to override; a Nay sustains the veto.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Tax Relief for Fraud Victims Act (H R 9500)
votes.bill_title: Tax Relief for Fraud Victims Act
votes.plain_language: This bill widens the tax deduction for theft and fraud losses, including losses that are not from a declared disaster, and it eases related refund and retirement-plan rules. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — IRS Whistleblower Program Improvement Act (H R 7959)
votes.bill_title: IRS Whistleblower Program Improvement Act
votes.plain_language: This bill modifies provisions of the Internal Revenue Code relating to whistleblower awards and protections. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — Expressing support for tax policies that support working families (H RES 1156)
votes.bill_title: Expressing support for tax policies that support working families.
votes.plain_language: This resolution expresses support for tax policies that support working families and recognizes the tax relief enacted as part of the 2025 reconciliation act. A Yea agrees to the resolution; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Passage — Removing Barriers to Work for Disabled Americans Act (H R 8884)
votes.bill_title: Removing Barriers to Work for Disabled Americans Act
votes.plain_language: This bill restarts Social Security disability demonstration projects through 2031 and says a participant's total income cannot be reduced. A Yea passes it. A Nay votes no.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Clergy Act (H R 227)
votes.bill_title: Clergy Act
votes.plain_language: This bill establishes a two-year window for certain members of the clergy and Christian Science practitioners to revoke their exemption from Social Security and Medicare taxes on ministerial earnings. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.
